text:
Gavin Brindley is back in Colorado because the worst week of the Avalanche season needed a body. Nathan MacKinnon (out at least a month) and Cale Makar (about two weeks) both went down with lower-body injuries in the same period in Ottawa on Nov. 12, and Brindley was recalled from the AHL the next day. He played 12 minutes in Saturday's 4-1 win in Montreal, tied for his most this season.

Expectations should stay modest. The 22-year-old has one assist in six games and four shots, and his rate of chances is well below last season's. He's small (5-foot-8) and quick, with a top speed in the 91st percentile in NHL Edge tracking, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him getting 67% of his exits out with possession last season.

Evolving-Hockey's note is the useful warning: last year he played with very strong teammates, which flatters his raw on-ice numbers. Without MacKinnon, nobody on this roster gets that cushion. A month of real minutes would tell us more than his first 63 NHL games have.
